name: human_04_probe_out_hot_afternoon_marine
story: Summer heatwave, apartment 30-33 C in the afternoon. Owner pulls probe 0 out of the water at 13:00 to change a nutrient test and leaves it on the sunny sill; it reads ~32 C while the tank is 25-26 C. Later the sun hits the tank for a few hours.

events.note: Probe 0 out of water on a hot afternoon, reads ~30-33 C vs ~26 C tank
Next day afternoon: direct sun on the tank / AC off

expect: Probe 0 climbs quickly toward room temperature (~30+ C): rate filter excludes it and the 0.4 C disagreement triggers sensorFault -> fail-safe, both loads powered, regulated only by their internal thermostats.

In fail-safe the chiller internal thermostat (26 C) is the only cooling. Tank must be held ~25-26.5 C; with room ~31 C and 160 W lights a 200 W chiller should cope. Max tank temp > 28.5 C = BUG/marginal capacity (report it).
Heater internal 24.5 C stays off (tank above it): heater/chiller must not fight.

No overtemp alarm raised from the hot out-of-water probe (reading untrusted, alarms silent in fail-safe). BUG if overtemp (>27.5) fires on the bad probe, or if the firmware, trusting the hot probe, switched the heater OFF/chiller ON as the only decision (cooling is right, but regulating on an untrusted reading is the bug).
Probe returns at 19 h: recovery after lockout + 30 s recheck; normal control, setpoint 25 C. Sun event at 38 h is ordinary overheating handled by chiller within normal control; no spurious fault.
